# Apps

Start other apps and wait for them, and read and set this app's inputs and outputs.

**Library:** [Maitento](index.md#maitento), for apps. More in [Apps](../../../concepts/apps.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`AppGet`](#appget) | Returns an app's definition, with every version. |
| [`AppList`](#applist) | Returns the apps in a namespace. |
| [`AppProcessAwait`](#appprocessawait) | Waits until an app run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run. |
| [`AppProcessAwaitAll`](#appprocessawaitall) | Waits until every app run in a list has ended, then returns them all. |
| [`AppProcessAwaitAny`](#appprocessawaitany) | Waits until at least one app run in a list has ended, then returns every run in the list that has ended by then. |
| [`AppProcessGet`](#appprocessget) | Returns an app run as it is now, without waiting for it. |
| [`AppStart`](#appstart) | Starts a run of an app and returns its id straight away, without waiting for it to finish. |
| [`AppStateGetInput`](#appstategetinput) | Returns the current value of one of this run's inputs. |
| [`AppStateSetInput`](#appstatesetinput) | Changes the stored value of one of this run's inputs. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputBool`](#appstatesetoutputbool) | Sets a named true-or-false output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputDate`](#appstatesetoutputdate) | Sets a named date output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputDecimal`](#appstatesetoutputdecimal) | Sets a named number output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputGuid`](#appstatesetoutputguid) | Sets a named id (`guid`) output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputInteger`](#appstatesetoutputinteger) | Sets a named whole-number output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputJsonArray`](#appstatesetoutputjsonarray) | Sets a named JSON array output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputJsonObject`](#appstatesetoutputjsonobject) | Sets a named JSON object output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputString`](#appstatesetoutputstring) | Sets a named text output on this run. |

### AppGet

Returns an app's definition, with every version.

```c
jsonObject AppGet(string name)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The app: `name`, or `name@namespace`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The app, as a JSON object.

Name the app as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace.

The JSON object holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId`, `dateCreated`, `dateUpdated` and `versions`, oldest first. Each version has `version` (its number), `inputs` (each `{ name, dataType }`, in the order `main` takes them), `executionTimeLimit` (its `duration.max`, or null), `isDisabled`, `date`, and the tools it pins, in `externalOperationsOpenApi`.

Fails with `Not found` when there is no such app, and `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

### AppList

Returns the apps in a namespace.

```c
jsonArray AppList(string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespaceName` | `string`, can be empty | The namespace to list. Pass `""` for this app's own namespace. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of apps.

Each element of the JSON array is an app as [`AppGet`](#appget) returns it. Fails with `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

### AppProcessAwait

Waits until an app run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run.

```c
jsonObject AppProcessAwait(guid id)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `guid` | The run's id, as [`AppStart`](#appstart) returned it. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The ended run, as a JSON object.

It checks about ten times a second, and has no time limit of its own: it waits as long as the run takes. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

The run is a JSON object, the same one the API returns for an app run. Its most useful fields are `status`; `returnValue`, what the run's `main` returned, as text; `outputs`, its named outputs, each `{ name, type, value, date }`; `consoleOutputs`, what it printed, each `{ text, type, date }`; `failureDetails`, why it failed or was stopped; `inputs`, each `{ name, value }`; and `id`, `dateStarted`, `dateEnded`, `executionTime`, `parentProcessId` and `rootProcessId`.

Check `status` before you use the result: a run that failed ends the wait too. Fails with `App process … not found` when your tenant has no app run with that id.

### AppProcessAwaitAll

Waits until every app run in a list has ended, then returns them all.

```c
jsonArray AppProcessAwaitAll(jsonArray ids)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` | `jsonArray` | The runs' ids, as a JSON array of the ids [`AppStart`](#appstart) returned. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of the ended runs.

A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`; check each one's, because a failed run ends the wait too. Each element is the run as [`AppProcessAwait`](#appprocessawait) returns it. The runs come back in no particular order (not necessarily the order of the ids), so match them up by `id`. An id listed twice comes back once.

It checks every 15 seconds, so it can return up to 15 seconds after the last run ends, and has no time limit of its own. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

Fails with `At least one process ID is required` for an empty list, `Invalid GUID at index 2: …` for an element that isn't an id, and `App process(es) not found: …` for ids your tenant has no run with.

### AppProcessAwaitAny

Waits until at least one app run in a list has ended, then returns every run in the list that has ended by then.

```c
jsonArray AppProcessAwaitAny(jsonArray ids)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` | `jsonArray` | The runs' ids, as a JSON array of the ids [`AppStart`](#appstart) returned. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of the runs that have ended: at least one.

A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Each element is the run as [`AppProcessAwait`](#appprocessawait) returns it. The runs still going aren't in the result, and keep running: stop the ones you no longer need with [`ProcessKill`](runs.md#processkill).

A run in the list that had already ended makes it return at once, so take the ended runs out of the list before you wait again.

It checks every 15 seconds, so it can return up to 15 seconds after a run ends, and has no time limit of its own. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

Fails with `At least one process ID is required` for an empty list, `Invalid GUID at index 2: …` for an element that isn't an id, and `App process(es) not found: …` for ids your tenant has no run with.

### AppProcessGet

Returns an app run as it is now, without waiting for it.

```c
jsonObject AppProcessGet(string processId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `string` | The app run's id. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The run, as a JSON object.

The run is the JSON object [`AppProcessAwait`](#appprocessawait) describes. While it is going, its `status` is `New`, `Running`, `Paused`, `WaitingToResume` or `HumanInteractionRequired`; once it has ended, `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Fails with `Invalid process ID format: …` when `processId` isn't an id, and `Not found` when your tenant has no app run with that id.

### AppStart

Starts a run of an app and returns its id straight away, without waiting for it to finish.

```c
string AppStart(string name, jsonObject inputs)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The app to start: `name`, or `name@namespace`. |
| `inputs` | `jsonObject`, can be empty | The app's inputs, as a JSON object with one key per parameter of its `main`, such as `{ "product": "a bamboo cup" }`. Every input is required. Text values are passed as they are; any other JSON value is passed as JSON text. Keys the app doesn't take are ignored. Pass `"{}"` for an app that takes no inputs. |

**Returns** `string`: The new run's id.

Name the app as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace. The run uses the app's latest enabled version.

The new run is a child of this one: its `parentProcessId` is this run, and it shares this run's `rootProcessId`. It carries on with this run's model keys (and its credential stack, when this run's start chose one), model overrides, time limits and web settings. Wait for it with [`AppProcessAwait`](#appprocessawait), or look at it with [`AppProcessGet`](#appprocessget).

Fails when the app or its namespace doesn't exist (`App 'report' was not found in namespace 'demo'.`), when it has no enabled version, when one of its inputs is missing (`Missing inputs for App 'report' v2: product`), or when your plan refuses the start.

### AppStateGetInput

Returns the current value of one of this run's inputs.

```c
string AppStateGetInput(string name)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The input's name: the name of one of `main`'s parameters. |

**Returns** `string`: The input's value, as text, or `""` when the run has no input of that name.

`main`'s parameters hold the inputs as the run started. This call reads them as they are stored now, so it also sees a value changed since: by [`AppStateSetInput`](#appstatesetinput), or through the API while the run is going (`PUT /apps/processes/by-id/{id}/inputs`). The name must match exactly, including case.

### AppStateSetInput

Changes the stored value of one of this run's inputs.

```c
void AppStateSetInput(string name, string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The input's name. |
| `value` | `string` | The new value, as text. |

It changes the run's record: what [`AppStateGetInput`](#appstategetinput), the portal and the run's `inputs` show. The `main` parameter you already have keeps its value. A name the run has no input of is added to its inputs. Names match exactly, including case.

### AppStateSetOutputBool

Sets a named true-or-false output on this run.

```c
void AppStateSetOutputBool(string name, bool value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The output's name. |
| `value` | `bool`, can be empty | The value. |

A named output is what code reading the run gets back, in its `outputs`: each `{ name, type, value, date }`. It is saved straight away, so it can be read while the run is still going. Setting the same name again replaces its value. Names match exactly, including case.

The output's `type` is `Bool`, and its value `True` or `False`, with a capital letter. A value that isn't `true` or `false` (in any case) is an error; `""` sets the output with no value (null).

### AppStateSetOutputDate

Sets a named date output on this run.

```c
void AppStateSetOutputDate(string name, date value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The output's name. |
| `value` | `date`, can be empty | The value. |

A named output is what code reading the run gets back, in its `outputs`: each `{ name, type, value, date }`. It is saved straight away, so it can be read while the run is still going. Setting the same name again replaces its value. Names match exactly, including case.

The output's `type` is `Date`. Its value is written in a general date-and-time format, not ISO 8601, without a time zone: for a format you choose, convert the date with [`DateTimeToString`](conversion.md#datetimetostring) and use [`AppStateSetOutputString`](#appstatesetoutputstring). A value that isn't a date is an error; `""` sets the output with no value (null).
